title: What is the World’s Oldest Civilisation?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: an advanced and organised society with cities, government, culture, and technology.
extra goods or food beyond what people need to survive.
a set of symbols used to record language and share information.
relating to cities or large, populated areas.
organised into levels of power, with some people higher than others.
the practice of farming and producing food.
unbroken over a long period of time

sentences.en: People love to debate history, especially when it comes to who was first.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢辩论历史，尤其是争论谁是第一的时候。

sentences.en: Last year, I made an episode about the oldest country in the world.
sentences.zh: 去年，我做过一期关于世界上最古老国家的播客。

sentences.en: I argued that the answer might be San Marino, because it has a long, continuous history as an independent state.
sentences.zh: 我当时提出，答案可能是圣马力诺，因为它作为一个独立国家，有着漫长而连贯的历史。

sentences.en: And the reaction from listeners was… quite intense!
sentences.zh: 听众们的反应可以说是……相当热烈！

sentences.en: I received comments from people around the world saying things like: “No, Egypt is older!” or “China has been around for thousands of years!” or “What about Iran?”.
sentences.zh: 我收到了来自世界各地听众的评论，他们说：“不对，埃及更古老！”或者“中国已经存在几千年了！”或者“那伊朗呢？”。

sentences.en: All of these arguments were interesting.
sentences.zh: 所有这些观点都很有趣。

sentences.en: But I think they were also missing something important: a country and a civilisation are not the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们也忽略了一个重要的问题：国家和文明并不是一回事。

sentences.en: So today, instead of talking about the oldest country, we’re asking a deeper question: What is the world’s oldest civilisation?
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我们不谈最古老的国家，而是要探讨一个更深层的问题：世界上最古老的文明是什么？

sentences.en: So, in today’s episode, we’ll explore these ancient cradles, find out what makes a civilisation, and decide whether there really is one society we can call “the oldest civilisation in the world,” all while learning some new English vocabulary!
sentences.zh: 因此，在今天的节目中，我们将探索这些古老的摇篮，了解究竟是什么造就了一个文明，并判断是否真的存在一个我们可以称之为“世界上最古老文明”的社会，同时还能学到一些新的英语词汇！

sentences.en: Before we can decide which civilization is the oldest, we need to understand what a civilization actually is.
sentences.zh: 在我们决定哪个文明最古老之前，我们需要先了解文明到底是什么。

sentences.en: Historians, archeologists, and anthropologists don’t always agree on one exact definition of a civilization.
sentences.zh: 历史学家、考古学家和人类学家对文明的精确定义并不总能达成一致。

sentences.en: Still, most experts would say that a civilization is an organized society with a few key features.
sentences.zh: 不过，大多数专家会认为，文明是一个具备几个关键特征的组织化社会。

sentences.en: For example, civilizations usually have cities where large groups of people live together; a government or some kind of political leadership; social structures, which means that people have different roles in the society; culture like religion, art, language, and technology; and often writing systems which allow them to record information.
sentences.zh: 例如，文明通常拥有人们聚居的大城市；政府或某种政治领导层；社会结构，这意味着人们在社会中扮演不同的角色；诸如宗教、艺术、语言和技术等文化；以及通常能让他们记录信息的书写系统。

sentences.en: When these different elements, these different features, come together, experts tend to say that smaller villages, communities, or societies become something more complex.
sentences.zh: 当这些不同的元素、这些不同的特征汇聚在一起时，专家们往往会认为较小的村庄、社区或社会变成了一种更复杂的东西。

sentences.en: This complex structure is a civilization.
sentences.zh: 这种复杂的结构就是一个文明。

sentences.en: Now, it’s really important to understand the difference between a “civilization” and a “country”, because this was the source of so many comments on that previous episode about the world’s oldest country.
sentences.zh: 现在，理解“文明”和“国家”之间的区别非常重要，因为这就是上一期关于世界上最古老国家的节目引发如此多评论的原因。

sentences.en: A country, as we understand it today, is a political entity with clearly defined borders.
sentences.zh: 正如我们今天所理解的那样，国家是一个具有清晰划定边界的政治实体。

sentences.en: It has a government, legal system and a national identity.
sentences.zh: 它拥有政府、法律体系和国家认同。

sentences.en: Countries are modern concepts. They’re not an ancient thing, they’re a modern thing.
sentences.zh: 国家是现代概念。它们不是古代的事物，而是现代的事物。

sentences.en: Even if their culture is ancient, the official country might still be relatively new.
sentences.zh: 即使它们的文化是古老的，官方的国家可能依然相对较新。

sentences.en: Like India has a culture that is thousands of years old, but the modern independent country of India was founded in 1947.
sentences.zh: 比如印度的文化有几千年的历史，但现代独立印度国成立于1947年。

sentences.en: A civilization is much broader. It doesn’t always have fixed borders, and it can exist when there is no one single government controlling everything.
sentences.zh: 文明要广阔得多。它并不总是有固定的边界，而且在没有单一政府控制一切的情况下也能存在。

sentences.en: It refers to the development of culture, society, technology, and ideas over a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 它指的是文化、社会、技术和思想在很长一段时间内的发展。

sentences.en: A civilization might include multiple kingdoms, some city states, even empires.
sentences.zh: 一个文明可能包括多个王国、一些城邦，甚至帝国。

sentences.en: And those political systems might rise and fall while the civilization continues.
sentences.zh: 而这些政治体制可能会兴衰交替，但文明却在延续。

sentences.en: So the question in this episode is not about modern borders or current governments, it’s about where organized human societies first started to grow into civilizations.
sentences.zh: 所以这期节目讨论的问题无关现代边界或现行政府，而是关于有组织的的人类社会最初是如何开始发展成为文明的。

sentences.en: And to answer that question, we need to look at the idea of “Cradles of Civilization “.
sentences.zh: 为了回答这个问题，我们需要审视“文明的摇篮”这个概念。

sentences.en: Cradle is the word we use for a baby’s bed.
sentences.zh: 摇篮是我们用来指婴儿床的词。

sentences.en: A cradle is the place where life begins.
sentences.zh: 摇篮是生命开始的地方。

sentences.en: So when we talk about the “cradle of civilization “, we are talking about the place, the places, where complex human societies were born.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们谈论“文明的摇篮”时，我们谈论的是复杂人类社会诞生的那个地方或那些地方。

sentences.en: This concept refers to specific regions in the ancient world where humans made a dramatic change in how they lived.
sentences.zh: 这个概念指的是古代世界中人类的生活方式发生戏剧性转变的特定区域。

sentences.en: Instead of moving from place to place as hunter gatherers or living in small farming villages, people in these areas began forming large organized communities.
sentences.zh: 这些人不再四处迁徙作为猎人采集者或居住在小型农耕村庄里，而是开始形成大型有组织的社区。

sentences.en: They built cities with thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 他们建造了拥有数千人的城市。

sentences.en: And importantly, many of them invented writing.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，他们中的许多人发明了文字。

sentences.en: Once you can write things down, it makes it so much easier for your society to grow and advance and for history to begin.
sentences.zh: 一旦你能把事情写下来，就会让你的社会更容易成长和进步，也让历史得以开始。

sentences.en: A “cradle of civilization” is where we see this complete change in human life.
sentences.zh: “文明的摇篮”就是我们见证人类生活发生这种彻底变革的地方。

sentences.en: Society becomes complex and structured. This could involve a few different things.
sentences.zh: 社会变得复杂且结构化。这可能涉及几个不同的方面。

sentences.en: People learn to farm in large organized ways.
sentences.zh: 人们学会以大规模、有组织的方式进行农业生产。

sentences.en: Food production becomes large enough to create surplus.
sentences.zh: 粮食产量变得足够大以创造盈余。

sentences.en: Surplus means more food than you need, which means that not everyone needs to be a farmer.
sentences.zh: 盈余意味着多于你所需体量的食物，这意味着并非每个人都需要成为农民。

sentences.en: Cities grow, bringing people together in urban communities for the first time.
sentences.zh: 城市不断发展，首次将人们聚集在城市社区中。

sentences.en: Leaders, laws and systems appear. They form governments and administration.
sentences.zh: 领导者、法律和体制随之出现。他们组成了政府和行政机构。

sentences.en: Society might be hierarchical. This means people have different occupations, classes, and roles.
sentences.zh: 社会可能是等级森严的。这意味着人们有不同的职业、阶层和角色。

sentences.en: People begin to record information, either through writing or other systems of storage.
sentences.zh: 人们开始记录信息，无论是通过文字还是其他存储系统。

sentences.en: And trade expands, spreading goods and ideas across the region.
sentences.zh: 贸易也随之扩张，将货物和思想传播到整个地区。

sentences.en: What’s incredible is that this didn’t happen in just one place.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的是，这并不是只在一个地方发生。

sentences.en: Different cultures around the world made this leap, this jump, independently without copying each other.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的不同文化在没有互相抄袭的情况下，各自独立地实现了这一飞跃。

sentences.en: They developed their own civilizations in their own ways.
sentences.zh: 他们以各自的方式发展出了自己的文明。

sentences.en: Historians now generally identify six regions where civilization first began.
sentences.zh: 历史学家现在普遍认同文明最早发源的六个地区。

sentences.en: Mesopotamia, which is modern Iraq and the surrounding region.
sentences.zh: 美索不达米亚，也就是现代的伊拉克及其周边地区。

sentences.en: Ancient Egypt, along the Nile River. The Indus Valley Civilization, which is now modern day Pakistan and Northwest India.
sentences.zh: 沿着尼罗河流域的古埃及。印度河流域文明，也就是现在的巴基斯坦和印度西北部。

sentences.en: Ancient China around the Yellow River region.
sentences.zh: 围绕黄河流域的古代中国。

sentences.en: Mesoamerica, for example the Olmec culture in modern Mexico.
sentences.zh: 中美洲，例如现代墨西哥的奥尔梅克文化。

sentences.en: And the Andean Civilizations like the Norte Chico in Peru.
sentences.zh: 以及秘鲁的小北等安第斯文明。

sentences.en: So let’s take a deeper look at each of these civilizations.
sentences.zh: 让我们更深入地了解这些文明中的每一个。

sentences.en: If we were forced to choose one place that looks the most like the first civilizations, many historians would probably point to Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 如果我们被迫选择一个最像最早文明的地方，许多历史学家可能会指向美索不达米亚。

sentences.en: Mesopotamia is a region that today lies mostly in Iraq, with parts of Syria, Turkey, Kuwait, and Iran.
sentences.zh: 美索不达米亚是一个今天主要位于伊拉克，并包含叙利亚、土耳其、科威特和伊朗部分地区的地区。

sentences.en: The name comes from Ancient Greek and literally means “the land between rivers “.
sentences.zh: 这个名字源自古希腊语，字面意思是“两河之间的土地”。

sentences.en: Those rivers were the Tigris and the Euphrates, and they were the reason civilization could grow there.
sentences.zh: 这两条河是底格里斯河和幼发拉底河，它们是文明能够在那里发展的原因。

sentences.en: Around 6,000 years ago, people living in that region began using the rivers to irrigate crops.
sentences.zh: 大约6000年前，生活在那里的居民开始利用河流来灌溉农作物。

sentences.en: Irrigation allows people to produce more food than they need by using the water from the rivers.
sentences.zh: 灌溉使人们能够利用河水生产出超过自身需求的粮食。

sentences.en: When a society has surplus food, more food than they need, not everyone has to be a farmer.
sentences.zh: 当一个社会有了粮食盈余，即超过所需的食物时，并非每个人都必须成为农民。

sentences.en: That means some people can focus on other tasks; building things, trading, making tools, studying astronomy, practicing religion, or being a leader.
sentences.zh: 这意味着有些人可以专注于其他任务；建造房屋、经商、制造工具、研究天文学、从事宗教活动或成为领导者。

sentences.en: Soon, small villages grew into the world’s first great cities.
sentences.zh: 很快，小村庄发展成了世界上第一批伟大的城市。

sentences.en: Uruk, possibly the first true city in history, may have had tens of thousands of people living there.
sentences.zh: 乌鲁克可能是历史上第一座真正的城市，当时可能有数万人居住在那里。

sentences.en: This is an enormous number in the ancient world.
sentences.zh: 在古代世界，这是一个庞大的数字。

sentences.en: These cities were crowded and busy, with large temples, markets for trade, and systems to manage taxes and laws.
sentences.zh: 这些城市拥挤而繁华，拥有宏大的神庙、用于贸易的市场以及管理税收和法律的系统。

sentences.en: Around 3,200 BCE, the Sumerians, one of the Mesopotamian kingdoms created a writing system called Cuneiform.
sentences.zh: 大约公元前3200年，美索不达米亚的王国之一苏美尔人创造了一种名为楔形文字的书写系统。

sentences.en: In Cuneiform, symbols are pressed into clay tablets with a stylus.
sentences.zh: 在楔形文字中，符号是用笔尖压印在泥板上的。

sentences.en: Writing first helped record trade and taxes, and then over time it expanded to poetry, religion, and science.
sentences.zh: 文字首先用于记录贸易和税收，随后逐渐扩展到诗歌、宗教和科学。

sentences.en: One of the oldest known stories in human history, the Epic of Gilgamesh, comes from Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 人类历史上最古老的故事之一《吉尔伽美什史诗》就源自美索不达米亚。

sentences.en: Mesopotamia also gave the world some of the earliest legal systems, including the Code of Hammurabi, which listed hundreds of laws with specific punishments.
sentences.zh: 美索不达米亚还为世界贡献了最早的一些法律体系，包括《汉谟拉比法典》，其中列出了数百条带有具体惩罚措施的法律。

sentences.en: Because of its early cities, complex government and the invention of writing, Mesopotamia is often called the world’s first civilization.
sentences.zh: 由于其早期的城市、复杂的政府和文字的发明，美索不达米亚通常被称为世界第一文明。

sentences.en: But it wasn’t the only one developing at that time.
sentences.zh: 但它并不是当时唯一在发展的文明。

sentences.en: Another civilization was rising along one of the most important rivers in human history, the Nile.
sentences.zh: 另一个文明正在人类历史上最重要的河流之一——尼罗河沿岸崛起。

sentences.en: The Ancient Egyptian civilization slowly grew along the banks of the Nile, where predictable flooding made farming possible.
sentences.zh: 古埃及文明沿着尼罗河岸边缓缓发展，规律的泛滥使农业成为可能。

sentences.en: Every year, the Nile flooded and left behind good soil for farming.
sentences.zh: 每年，尼罗河都会泛滥并留下肥沃的土壤用于农业。

sentences.en: This meant farmers could grow more food than they needed, and just like in Mesopotamia, a surplus of food allowed society to become more complex.
sentences.zh: 这意味着农民可以种植出超过所需的粮食，就像在美索不达米亚一样，粮食盈余使社会变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: Around 3,100 BCE, smaller kingdoms along the Nile were unified under a single ruler, traditionally believed to be King Namar.
sentences.zh: 大约公元前3100年，尼罗河流域较小的王国在单一统治者的统治下统一，传统上认为这位统治者是纳尔迈国王。

sentences.en: The union created one of the longest lasting civilizations the world has ever seen.
sentences.zh: 这一联合创造了世界上持续时间最长的文明之一。

sentences.en: Egyptian civilization is famous for its architecture, especially the pyramids.
sentences.zh: 埃及文明以其建筑闻名于世，尤其是金字塔。

sentences.en: These massive structures were impressive and elaborate tombs, designed to protect the Pharaohs ‘, the Egyptian king’s, bodies and help their soul travel to the afterlife.
sentences.zh: 这些宏伟的建筑是令人惊叹且复杂的陵墓，旨在保护法老（埃及国王）的遗体并帮助他们的灵魂前往来世。

sentences.en: Constructing them required advanced engineering, mathematics, and thousands of skilled workers.
sentences.zh: 建造它们需要先进的工程学、数学和数千名熟练工人。

sentences.en: It also required government organization capable of planning and feeding and managing labor forces.
sentences.zh: 它还需要能够规划、供给和管理劳动力的政府组织能力。

sentences.en: The Egyptians also developed hieroglyphics, one of the earliest writing systems.
sentences.zh: 埃及人还开发了象形文字，这是最早的书写系统之一。

sentences.en: Hieroglyphs used pictures and symbols to represent sounds, ideas, and objects.
sentences.zh: 象形文字使用图画和符号来表示声音、思想和物体。

sentences.en: Writing was used for religion and trade and administration, and even history.
sentences.zh: 文字被用于宗教、贸易、行政管理甚至是历史记录。

sentences.en: Through writing, Egypt preserved stories about Gods and Pharaohs and also people’s everyday life.
sentences.zh: 通过文字，埃及保存了关于神灵、法老以及人们日常生活的故事。

sentences.en: While Mesopotamian cities often fought wars against each other, Egypt tended to be a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 虽然美索不达米亚的城市经常互相发动战争，但埃及往往有些不同。

sentences.en: Its geography protected it. There were deserts on both sides, the sea of the north and the river at its center.
sentences.zh: 它的地理环境保护了它。它两边都是沙漠，北面是海洋，中心是一条河流。

sentences.en: This isolation encouraged a long and consistent cultural tradition.
sentences.zh: 这种孤立的环境孕育了漫长而连贯的文化传统。

sentences.en: However, Egypt was not isolated forever.
sentences.zh: 然而，埃及并没有永远处于世外桃源。

sentences.en: It definitely traded with its neighbors, exchanged goods and ideas and influenced societies across Africa and the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 它绝对与邻国进行过贸易，交换物资和思想，并影响了整个非洲和地中海的社会。

sentences.en: Far to the east of Mesopotamia and Egypt, another civilization flourished along the banks of two major rivers: the Indus and the Saraswati (which is a river Scholars believe was once a great river, but has since dried up.)
sentences.zh: 在美索不达米亚和埃及以东的远方，另一个文明在两条主要河流的岸边繁荣发展：印度河和萨拉斯瓦蒂河（学者们认为这条河曾经是一条大河，但后来已经干涸）。

sentences.en: The ancient society existed in what is now Pakistan and Northwest India, and is probably one of history’s most intriguing mysteries.
sentences.zh: 这个古代社会存在于现在的巴基斯坦和印度西北部，可能是历史上最令人着迷的谜团之一。

sentences.en: The Indus Valley Civilization began developing around 3,300 BCE, and it reached its peak maybe around 2,600 BCE to 1,900 BCE.
sentences.zh: 印度河流域文明大约在公元前3300年开始发展，并在大约公元前2600年至公元前1900年达到顶峰。

sentences.en: The cities of the Indus Valley were very advanced, perhaps even more advanced than those in Mesopotamia or Egypt during the same period.
sentences.zh: 印度河流域的城市非常先进，甚至可能比同期美索不达米亚或埃及的城市还要先进。

sentences.en: Cities like Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro were built on a grid system.
sentences.zh: 像哈拉帕和摩亨佐-达罗这样的城市都是按网格系统建造的。

sentences.en: They had straight streets intersecting at right angles.
sentences.zh: 它们拥有呈直角相交的笔直街道。

sentences.en: They had complex drainage and sewage systems that ran underneath the streets.
sentences.zh: 它们拥有在街道下方运行的复杂的排水和排污系统。

sentences.en: This is something that wouldn’t appear in many parts of the world for thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 这在世界许多地方是几千年后才出现的东西。

sentences.en: Houses were made of bricks of standard sizes, which suggests that there was some kind of central planning.
sentences.zh: 房屋是用标准尺寸的砖块建造的，这表明存在某种中央集权规划。

sentences.en: In fact, some historians argue that no ancient civilization was better at urban planning than the Indus Valley.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一些历史学家认为，没有任何古代文明在城市规划上能超过印度河流域。

sentences.en: Trade was a major part of life in the Indus Valley.
sentences.zh: 贸易是印度河流域生活的主要部分。

sentences.en: Archeologists have found tools and jewelry and pottery, and also seals used for commerce.
sentences.zh: 考古学家发现了工具、珠宝和陶器，以及用于商业的印章。

sentences.en: These seals often show animals and symbols, which appears to be a writing system.
sentences.zh: 这些印章通常显示动物和符号，这似乎是一种书写系统。

sentences.en: But no one has ever been able to fully decipher the Indus script.
sentences.zh: 但是没有人能够完全破译印度河文字。

sentences.en: Without being able to read the writing of the Indus Valley, we know far less about them than we know about Egypt or Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 由于无法阅读印度河流域的文字，我们对他们的了解远少于对埃及或美索不达米亚的了解。

sentences.en: We don’t know if they had kings. We don’t know if they worshiped gods.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道他们是否有国王。我们不知道他们是否崇拜神明。

sentences.en: And we don’t know how their society was ruled.
sentences.zh: 我们也不知道他们的社会是如何被统治的。

sentences.en: There are no enormous palaces or giant temples.
sentences.zh: 那里没有巨大的宫殿或巨大的神庙。

sentences.en: Instead, their cities seem very organized.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们的城市显得非常有条理。

sentences.en: Some historians have suggested that power might have been decentralized.
sentences.zh: 一些历史学家提出，权力可能是分散的。

sentences.en: Maybe there was no one king, but we just don’t know.
sentences.zh: 也许没有唯一的国王，但我们只是无从得知。

sentences.en: Despite the mystery, the people of the valley were clearly skilled in trade and technology, and of course, city planning.
sentences.zh: 尽管存在神秘感，但流域的人民显然精通贸易、技术，当然还有城市规划。

sentences.en: We also know that they traded with Mesopotamia by sea.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道他们曾通过海上与美索不达米亚进行贸易。

sentences.en: But around the year 1,900 BCE, their civilization declined.
sentences.zh: 但在公元前1900年左右，他们的文明衰落了。

sentences.en: The reasons are not really known. Perhaps it was climate change.
sentences.zh: 原因其实并不为人所知。也许是气候变化。

sentences.en: Maybe the rivers shifted. Or their trade networks collapsed.
sentences.zh: 也许是河流改道。或者他们的贸易网络崩溃了。

sentences.en: As the Indus Civilization was growing and transforming, another ancient society was also beginning on the banks of a river further east.
sentences.zh: 正当印度河流域文明在成长和蜕变时，另一个古代社会也开始在更东边的一条河流岸边兴起。

sentences.en: This river was the Yellow River in modern day China.
sentences.zh: 这条河就是现代中国的黄河。

sentences.en: This is also a very fertile region, which saw the rise of farming communities thousands of years ago.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个非常肥沃的地区，几千年前就见证了农耕社区的崛起。

sentences.en: Around the year 2000 BCE, these communities had grown into societies.
sentences.zh: 大约在公元前2000年，这些社区已经发展成了社会。

sentences.en: Eventually, the societies formed one of the world’s longest continuous civilizations.
sentences.zh: 最终，这些社会形成了世界上持续时间最长的文明之一。

sentences.en: The Yellow River is often called the Mother River of China.
sentences.zh: 黄河常被称为中国的母亲河。

sentences.en: Its rich soil made agriculture possible.
sentences.zh: 它肥沃的土壤使农业成为可能。

sentences.en: This river, however, was far more unpredictable than the rivers in Egypt and Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 然而，这条河比埃及和美索不达米亚的河流要难以预测得多。

sentences.en: The Yellow Rivers floods were sometimes violent and destructive.
sentences.zh: 黄河的洪水有时是暴力且具有破坏性的。

sentences.en: Managing the river required cooperation and planning, and maybe this need for organization may have helped early rulers establish political authority and eventually a civilization.
sentences.zh: 治理这条河流需要合作与规划，也许这种对组织的需求帮助了早期统治者确立政治权威并最终形成了文明。

sentences.en: Archeological evidence points to several early cultures and dynasties, including the Xia dynasty (which some historians debate whether it really existed), followed by the more clearly documented Shang Dynasty, around 1,600 BCE.
sentences.zh: 考古证据指向几个早期文化和朝代，包括夏朝（一些历史学家对它是否真的存在争论不休），随后是公元前1600年左右有更清晰文献记载的商朝。

sentences.en: The Shang rulers controlled territory, they had armies and they performed religious rituals.
sentences.zh: 商朝统治者控制领土，他们拥有军队并举行宗教仪式。

sentences.en: They also produced some of the earliest evidence of Chinese writing.
sentences.zh: 他们还生产了中国最早的书写证据。

sentences.en: We have found these symbols carved into animal bones and turtle shells.
sentences.zh: 我们在动物骨头和乌龟壳上发现了这些刻下的符号。

sentences.en: This early writing system eventually evolved into modern Chinese writing.
sentences.zh: 这个早期的书写系统最终演变成为了现代汉字。

sentences.en: Rituals, ancestor worship, respect for hierarchy, and the idea that rulers governed with the approval of the gods were all central ideas in Ancient China.
sentences.zh: 仪式、祖先崇拜、对等级制度的尊重，以及统治者凭借神明批准进行统治的观念，都是中国古代的核心思想。

sentences.en: Later, these concepts evolved into modern Chinese philosophy and beliefs.
sentences.zh: 后来，这些概念演变成了现代的中国哲学和信仰。

sentences.en: Chinese civilization also made advances in technology and crafts like bronze and silk production, pottery and early mathematics.
sentences.zh: 中国文明还在青铜和丝绸生产、陶器以及早期数学等技术和工艺上取得了进步。

sentences.en: Cities grew and economies expanded, and over the centuries, many different dynasties rose and fell.
sentences.zh: 城市不断发展，经济不断扩张，在过去的几个世纪里，许多不同的朝代兴衰更替。

sentences.en: But despite this, China maintained a remarkably continuous cultural identity.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，中国依然保持了惊人连贯的文化认同。

sentences.en: While kingdoms collapsed and governments changed, and the civilization’s borders expanded and contracted, Chinese writing, art, philosophy and traditions have stayed connected across thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 虽然王国崩塌、政府更迭，文明的边界时而扩张时而收缩，但中国的文字、艺术、哲学和传统在数千年的时间里始终保持着联系。

sentences.en: This sets China apart from many of the other cradles of civilization.
sentences.zh: 这使得中国与其他许多文明摇篮区别开来。

sentences.en: Today it is sometimes claimed that China is the oldest continuous civilization, and I think there is definitely truth in that idea.
sentences.zh: 今天，有时有人声称中国是最古老的连续文明，我认为这个观点绝对有其道理。

sentences.en: You can trace modern China back to the same China that existed 2000 or 3000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 你可以将现代中国追溯到2000或3000年前存在的那个中国。

sentences.en: On the opposite side of the world, complex civilizations also began to emerge in the region we now call Mesoamerica.
sentences.zh: 在地球的另一端，复杂的文明也开始在我们现在称为中美洲的地区涌现。

sentences.en: This is an area that includes modern Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, parts of Honduras and El Salvador.
sentences.zh: 这是一个包括现代墨西哥、危地马拉、伯利兹、洪都拉斯和萨尔瓦多部分地区的区域。

sentences.en: What makes Mesoamerica remarkable is that its civilizations developed independently.
sentences.zh: 中美洲非凡的地方在于其文明是独立发展的。

sentences.en: They didn’t learn farming from the Middle East or writing from China.
sentences.zh: 他们没有从中东学习农业，也没有从中国学习文字。

sentences.en: They created their own systems from the ground up.
sentences.zh: 他们从零开始建立了自己的系统。

sentences.en: The very first known civilization in this region was the Olmec, beginning around 1,600 to 1,400 BCE.
sentences.zh: 该地区最早为人所知的文明是奥尔梅克，始于大约公元前1600年至公元前1400年。

sentences.en: The Olmec are often called the mother culture of Mesoamerica because many later societies including the Maya, Zapotec and the Aztec (which I have an episode on… the history of Mexico City), inherited aspects of their art, religion, and political organization from the Olmec.
sentences.zh: 奥尔梅克通常被称为中美洲的母亲文化，因为许多后来的社会，包括玛雅人、萨波特克人和阿兹特克人（我做过一期关于墨西哥城历史的播客），都从奥尔梅克那里继承了他们的艺术、宗教和政治组织的各个方面。

sentences.en: The Olmec constructed ceremonial centers with large platforms, plazas and temples.
sentences.zh: 奥尔梅克人建造了带有大型平台、广场和神庙的礼仪中心。

sentences.en: What they are most famous for today is their enormous stone heads.
sentences.zh: 他们今天最著名的作品是他们巨大的石头头像。

sentences.en: These are giant sculptures weighing up to 50 tons and possibly represent their rulers.
sentences.zh: 这些巨大的雕塑重达50吨，可能代表了他们的统治者。

sentences.en: Farmers cultivated crops like maize (which is corn), beans, squash, and chili peppers.
sentences.zh: 农民种植了诸如玉米（也就是玉米）、豆类、南瓜和辣椒等农作物。

sentences.en: But instead of relying on river floods like Egypt or Mesopotamia, Mesoamerican societies developed complex techniques to deal with forests and hills and wetlands.
sentences.zh: 但中美洲社会没有依靠像埃及或美索不达米亚那样的河流泛滥，而是开发了复杂的技艺来应对森林、山丘和湿地。

sentences.en: As societies grew, they also developed writing systems.
sentences.zh: 随着社会的发展，他们也发展出了书写系统。

sentences.en: The Maya script, which appeared later, is the most fully developed writing system in the Americas, but the Olmec may have used earlier forms of writing and recordkeeping too.
sentences.zh: 后来出现的玛雅文字是美洲最完整的书写系统，但奥尔梅克人可能也使用过早期形式的文字和记录保存方式。

sentences.en: They created a calendar system and they made significant advances in astronomy and mathematics.
sentences.zh: 他们创建了历法系统，并在天文学和数学方面取得了重大进展。

sentences.en: But Mesoamerica wasn’t the only complex civilization in the Americas.
sentences.zh: 但中美洲并不是美洲唯一的复杂文明。

sentences.en: Further south on the Pacific coast of Peru, an even older culture grew.
sentences.zh: 更南边的秘鲁太平洋海岸，孕育了一种更古老的文化。

sentences.en: These ancient societies, known collectively as the Andean Civilizations, began long before the rise of the famous Inca Empire.
sentences.zh: 这些被称为安第斯文明的古代社会，在著名的印加帝国崛起之前很久就已经开始了。

sentences.en: Their origins stretch back over 5,000 years, making them among the oldest civilizations in the world.
sentences.zh: 他们的起源可以追溯到5000多年前，使他们成为世界上最古老的文明之一。

sentences.en: They also developed technology and society in a completely different way from the river based cultures of Africa, Europe, and Asia.
sentences.zh: 他们在技术和社会的发展方式上也完全不同于非洲、欧洲和亚洲以河流为基础的文化。

sentences.en: One of of the earliest and most surprising of these cultures was the Norte Chico, also called Caral, which dates from around 3000 BCE to 1,800 BCE.
sentences.zh: 这些文化中最早且最令人惊讶的文化之一是小北文化，也被称为卡拉尔，其历史可追溯至公元前3000年至公元前1800年左右。

sentences.en: What makes this culture remarkable is that it challenges all of our assumptions about what a civilization needs to survive.
sentences.zh: 这种文化引人注目之处在于，它挑战了我们对文明生存所需条件的所有假设。

sentences.en: These people did not rely on large scale agriculture of grains.
sentences.zh: 这些人并不依赖大规模的谷物农业。

sentences.en: Most societies had a grain, wheat or rice or maize, but in Peru, they did not have some kind of basic grain.
sentences.zh: 大多数社会都有一种谷物，小麦、大米或玉米，但在秘鲁，他们没有某种基础谷物。

sentences.en: They also had no evidence of a writing system.
sentences.zh: 他们也没有任何书写系统的证据。

sentences.en: Instead, they built their society around things like fishing.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们围绕着诸如捕鱼之类的事情来建立他们的社会。

sentences.en: The cities of Norte Chico featured platform mounds and plazas and large ceremonial structures, which suggest a kind of religion and leadership.
sentences.zh: 小北的城市以平台土墩、广场和大型礼仪建筑为特征，这暗示了某种宗教和领导层。

sentences.en: They had complex irrigation systems that supported agriculture.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有支持农业的复杂灌溉系统。

sentences.en: Interestingly, they don’t seem to have had much pottery or art.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他们似乎没有太多的陶器或艺术品。

sentences.en: But their architecture reveals a high level of social organization.
sentences.zh: 但他们的建筑展现了高度的社会组织能力。

sentences.en: Later Andean cultures built on these foundations.
sentences.zh: 后来的安第斯文化建立在这些基础之上。

sentences.en: They constructed religious centers high in the Andes mountains.
sentences.zh: 他们在安第斯山脉的高处建造了宗教中心。

sentences.en: These societies created trade networks, bringing together coastal, highland and jungle communities.
sentences.zh: 这些社会建立了贸易网络，将沿海、高原和丛林社区连接在一起。

sentences.en: Over thousands of years, Andean civilizations built farms on mountain slopes, developed irrigation systems, and grew crops like potatoes and quinoa.
sentences.zh: 在数千年的时间里，安第斯文明在山坡上修建农田，开发灌溉系统，并种植马铃薯和藜麦等作物。

sentences.en: Without the wheel for transport or any large animals for pulling carts, they still managed to create complex societies.
sentences.zh: 在没有用于运输的轮子或任何用于拉车的巨型动物的情况下，他们仍然设法创造了复杂的社会。

sentences.en: And while they didn’t really have writing, Andean cultures used a different method of keeping records.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们并没有真正的文字，但安第斯文化使用了一种不同的记录方法。

sentences.en: They used knotted strings. These knotted strings stored information.
sentences.zh: 他们使用打结的绳子。这些打结的绳子储存了信息。

sentences.en: Instead of writing with symbols or letters, they recorded numbers, maybe even stories using different colors, lengths, and types of knot.
sentences.zh: 他们不是用符号或字母书写，而是用不同的颜色、长度和结的类型来记录数字，甚至可能是故事。

sentences.en: The greatest expression, or the most famous version, of the Andean civilization came with the Inca Empire, which ruled over millions of people in South America.​
sentences.zh: 安第斯文明最伟大的表现形式，或者说最著名的版本，随着统治了南美数百万人的印加帝国的出现而到来。

sentences.en: After listening to today’s episode, hopefully you now understand that the question, “what is the world’s oldest civilization?” doesn’t have a single or simple answer.
sentences.zh: 听完今天的节目后，希望你现在明白“什么是世界上最古老的文明？”这个问题并没有单一或简单的答案。

sentences.en: It depends on how you choose to measure oldest.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你选择如何衡量“最古老”。

sentences.en: If we judge by the first large urban societies with writing, then Mesopotamia is usually considered the earliest.
sentences.zh: 如果我们以拥有文字的第一批大型城市社会来判断，那么美索不达米亚通常被认为是诞生最早的。

sentences.en: Cities like Uruk emerged over 5,000 years ago, along with the world’s first confirmed writing system.
sentences.zh: 像乌鲁克这样的城市在5000多年前就出现了，同时伴随着世界上第一个得到证实的书写系统。

sentences.en: But also around the same time, about 5,000 years ago in South America, the Andean civilizations were also building their first cities.
sentences.zh: 但大约在同一时期，即大约5000年前的南美洲，安第斯文明也在建造他们的第一座城市。

sentences.en: We just know a lot less about them. But if we focus on continuous civilization.
sentences.zh: 只是我们对他们的了解要少得多。但如果我们关注的是连续不断的文明。

sentences.en: A culture that has evolved but never completely disappeared, then China is a strong contender.
sentences.zh: 一个已经演变但从未完全消失的文化，那么中国是一个强有力的竞争者。

sentences.en: China has thousands of years of recognizable cultural tradition and language and historical records.
sentences.zh: 中国拥有数千年可识别的文化传统、语言和历史记载。

sentences.en: Maybe it’s more interesting to ask a different question.
sentences.zh: 也许提出一个不同的问题会更有趣。

sentences.en: Why do we want to know which civilization was first?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们想要知道哪个文明是第一？

sentences.en: History is not a competition. These ancient societies didn’t race to build pyramids or invent writing.
sentences.zh: 历史不是一场比赛。这些古代社会并没有竞相建造金字塔或发明文字。

sentences.en: They each developed according to their own local needs, their own environment, and their own ideas, their own creativity.
sentences.zh: 它们各自根据当地的需求、自身的环境、各自的想法以及自身的创造力进行发展。

sentences.en: But what do you think?
sentences.zh: 但你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Which is the oldest civilization? Did I miss something in today’s episode?
sentences.zh: 哪个是最古老的文明？我今天节目里漏掉了什么吗？
